paragraphs.text: overgo improves models, and itself, through its own inference and training, unattended. Every row closes or speeds up the improvement loop (measure, find the gap, train or change, judge on held-out data), or directly serves inference or training; otherwise it is not filed. The scorecard's gaps generate the work. Progress is each scorecard cell against its previous measurement, not a count of landings: there is no passed state and no promotion. Rows that let a full measurement run finish rank above rows that only harden or slim it, and a run that cannot finish (killed, or with cells that did not pass) outranks every other row.

Finish partly landed rows before opening new ones. A consolidation reuses an existing package and deletes the implementations it replaces in the same landing. A new shared component is allowed only when no existing package can serve several real consumers, and it must remove more than it adds.

One meaningful run serves every obligation whose identity and contract match: it is written once, as one record with many readers. A run never judges what it produced, and a run leaves its evidence complete by its own contract (every protocol a suite's acceptance asks for), never half-written for a later landing to trip on.

The landing gate judges the commit; the improvement cycle judges the models. The gate's verdict depends only on the tree: unit, golden, hermetic-fixture and small-device checks. Suites that load real models, read the live store's evidence or sweep the device belong to the cycle, declared by build tag, and the cycle runs them on the commit it measures; a store write never changes a landing's verdict. A change's landing cost is read from its diff as three independent effects: the lanes it reaches, whether it expires the inference-surface guards, and whether it needs a pinned-media reconciliation. Lanes are the main cost, so false lane reach is cut. A surface move also expires every evaluation bound to the surface, so the re-evaluation it forces counts in its cost: surface changes are batched and land before an evaluation run, never between its runs, and the guards are re-acquired once after the last of them. A batch is one coherent change, normally one to three related rows, closed before it delays a served result that is ready: an operating limit, not a gate. Dependency work is verified twice, separately: its build and test closure, and the guard surface, which stops at overgodb and runrecord. A saving is the net recurring cost removed, after the replacement tests and their maintenance. A check retires only when its replacement covers the check's actual acceptance contract, whether it moves to the cycle or is deleted; the landing scorecard reports and never refuses, so it replaces no check. The gate writes all numbers; messages name causes, effects and what disappears.

A step's verify fails before the change and passes after; a verify that already passes proves nothing, so a boundary is proved by the table row that fails today. Before a landing, what the gate refuses cheaply is run locally first: the claims check after any hand edit, the invariant tables, the rules' budget and exports, and the step's verify. A refusal found after the lanes costs an hour, and a retried landing rebuilds an identical gate binary.

Each row's rationale carries four plain lines: Serves (the loop stage, or the model or capability it runs or trains), Disappears (the package reused, the implementations deleted, the tests retired or kept), Evidence (the run and record it reads or produces, and who else reads that record), Batch (the lanes its diff reaches, whether it expires the guards, and whether it needs a media reconciliation: three independent effects, each checked against the diff).

Landing speed is protected by observing it, not by a rule. Each structural boundary (a changed path's lanes, a package kept off the inference surface, a suite kept to the cycle) is pinned as an invariant row in one table per kind, never as a new test function or a snapshot of today's lists. At each periodic review the gate's measured lines in git log are read: the share of landings that reached no lane, lane minutes per landing, and executed versus cached package counts. A rise means a misplaced check or a new false reach, fixed by moving it and adding a table row. There are no time budgets or timeouts, no ratchet baselines, and no separate tracking subsystem.

Training research is measured at the lowest cost that answers the question, reusing what exists. Optimizer math stays on the device: host Muon on the tied embedding cost about 98 s a step, and moving it took a 540-step run from about 21 hours to 6 minutes. During training only scalars cross to the host (losses, norms, brake decisions), never weights or gradients per step. Reuse comes before acquiring: cached base losses keyed by the exact window plan, existing checkpoints, held-out sets and the verdict code, before any new dataset, pass or tool. An evaluation beats a training run, a norm beats a decomposition, and a one-time computation beats a per-step one. For a training rate question the order is: post-hoc tests on existing checkpoints, then the held-out brake from the training forward against cached base losses, then a per-layer relative step size, and per-direction spectral scaling last.

Journey performance. Optimize complete journeys, measured as action to usable result: submit to first visible answer, cold model selection to usable response, cancel to actual resource release, interrupted cycle to useful progress, with loading, admission wait, execution, publication and rendering kept apart. Start from the existing native benchmarks, allocation counts and CPU profiles of repeated reads, model loads, allocations and evidence reconstruction, and keep added instrumentation only when it explains a real elapsed-time gain. In the development loop one valid gate execution is shared by every compatible plan step and obligation, and validation and reuse are scoped by the actual dependencies (kernels, generated and embedded data, models, recipes, environment, subprocess effects); an unknown dependency keeps the broader coverage. A gain is judged against total maintenance cost (production code, tests, fixtures, instrumentation, gate work and upkeep): remove repeated processing through existing packages, and decline small gains that need disproportionate machinery. Prove with behavioral regression tests and comparable benchmarks, never a new performance ratchet, selector or framework.

Pace. Steps that change one mechanism land together. A measurement already taken retires the step that would take it. Work that only waits is filed early, so its wait runs while the rows between are built. A full measurement run (go run ./cmd/loop -improve) continues only at the commit it began at and is started outside a session, so no time limit ends it. Rows that move no measured result land while it runs; rows that change a served result or a timing follow it, stand side by side, and land before the next run, never between its runs.

The repository keeps Go, CUDA and HTML/JS, and extends an existing package before it adds one. Each row begins with a measurement and fixes its acceptance before its code is written; a measurement already taken is reused when it is enough. A row deletes the implementation it replaces in the same landing; a reader that records already in the store need stays until those records are migrated. A pilot that is not accepted is taken out of the served path, and its measurements and the reason it was refused are kept.

The production growth refusal stays. A row with no count adds no net production code, which is the default: a migration deletes at least what it adds. A row that adds a mechanism before it deletes one carries a count, set in a change to the plan alone before its code, from the figure the gate's preflight gives its built change, and read from the commit the change builds on; a count set before the row is built is an estimate and says so. An item's count is for all its landings together: each landing's growth is charged to it and what is left is what the next may add. Test code, fixtures, record schemas and CUDA source are reported with each landing and not refused; a test is retired only when its replacement catches the same seeded failure.

The gate judges the candidate tree by hermetic and small-device checks; real-model quality and speed are measured by the cycle. A stored result is reused only under an unchanged identity of the code, model, recipe, data, settings and request it depends on. A request for a fresh measurement always runs, and a dependency that cannot be named keeps the wider scope. Resident resources, compiled execution and a request have separate identities, built by one mechanism into separate keys for sessions, outputs and scores. Eligibility is kept apart from selection, observations from scores, and the records that choose a candidate from the records that confirm it.

An experiment is frozen before it trains: a protocol missing a numerical gain or resource criterion is not dispatched, and a pilot does not change the acceptance of the objective it is compared with. Completing an experiment and adopting its model are separate: a complete negative or inconclusive record closes the experiment and activates nothing.

Order: the campaign runs in two phases, the release and then the Strata decode port.

Each unit is held to our reference by a parity test, greedy decoding being the exact oracle and sampled decoding held to its distribution, and judged by the bench suite against Strata over three alternating rounds.
A cost found in our loop is first read in Strata's source, and a probe answers only what the source does not.
A step takes at most two landings that only record measurements before it lands code or is retired, and a port that does not beat what it replaces is retired with its gap recorded, not attempted again.

steps.title: Admit the tensor-core prompt attention for Flash-Next through its architecture profile
steps.verify: go test ./internal/model -run '^TestPromptTensorCoresAdmittedPerArchitecture$' -count=1 && go test ./internal/modelrecipe ./internal/inferencesurface -count=1 && go test ./internal/evaluation -run '^TestQwenSmallRetainedTextAcceptance$' -count=1
steps.rationale:
Serves: Flash-Next's first output at length, 6 to 10 percent slower in the record of 2026-10-25 with the tensor-core prompt attention off (4K 1.50 to 1.66 s, 16K 5.23 to 5.54 s, against Strata's 2.2 and 5.0) although its MMLU-Pro held 0.6245 with the kernel on and without (the records of 2026-10-19 and 10-24), where gemma-4-12B-it-fp8's BBH fell under it.
Build: the architecture profile's runtime policy gains PromptTensorCores, set for qwen4exp alone in architecture_profiles.json, and the block builder passes it to each dense causal attention node as its TensorCores attribute (three sites in block.go). The gate holds serving code to selecting nothing by an architecture name (TestServingCodeNamesNoArchitecture refused a spec constant, 2026-10-25), and a profile field moves the catalog, fact and fact-schema digests TestProfileProvenanceHasExactTypedCoverage and TestRegisteredProfileSemanticDigest pin, and the provenance coverage of every stored profile document, which TestQwenSmallRetainedTextAcceptance reads from the store: the registered models' definitions are republished with the new profile documents before the field lands, through the activation path, never by hand-editing records.
Disappears: nothing; every other architecture keeps the f32 paths.

Serves: more tokens a window (the one-draft window carries 1.7 against Strata's 2.4).

Decision: the chain lands only if, over three alternating rounds against the one-draft window at its best, it decodes the bench suite's chat and agent cells faster, greedy and sampled; inside the rounds' ranges or slower, this step is retired with its measurements, parity records the agent-turn gap with its measured cause, and no further chained-draft attempt is filed. Map (2026-10-25, Strata at 296b59d2): Strata drafts a window from its MTP layer in a chain (src/core/mtp.cpp: mtp_draft runs up to max_steps drafts from the pending token, each step's draft the next step's input, and stops when a draft's probability falls under min_p; MtpDrafter::record_front, record_rest and capture_prefill capture the drafter's graphs, set_draft_sampling and set_draft_history couple it to a sampled request). The draft policy prices a window size by its measured round time (src/spec/draft_policy.cpp: an EMA of the round cost a size, a shape table for sizes not yet measured, a bucketed rate for lookup matches) and the suffix drafter fills a window from a stretch of the context the text repeats (src/spec/suffix_drafter.cpp; generate.cpp's suffix_draft = 3, mtp_max_t and chain_tail); generate.cpp's --mtp-min-p gates the drafts, 0.5 as benched.
